## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Scope candidates are generated by the machine entry

The Feature scope candidate SHALL be produced by a machine entry (`goal-mode-entry --prepare-scope`), never hand-written. The main agent SHALL supply exactly four inputs: the completion target, the requested results, the explicit requested action (expressed as `requested_phases`), and the impact judgement together with its source paths. Everything else — input bindings, their dependencies and `content_fingerprint`, the unit/device/visual evidence duties and the automatic `code-review` duty — SHALL be computed by the existing production resolvers, and every binding in the candidate SHALL be byte-identical to what `resolveCapabilityInputs` returns for the same input, so the freeze-time re-resolve cannot disagree with it.

`implementation` SHALL be decided by the requested action, never by `completion_target`: a request whose phases include an implementation provider carries the implementation duty with its declared write set as the source, and a verification-only request carries none. A request that includes an implementation phase without a verifiable write set SHALL be refused at generation time rather than deferred to coding. The write set SHALL be authorised only by the declared design contract; a write-set binding the candidate carries for itself is a self-report and SHALL NOT authorise anything. A design artifact that exists but declares no verifiable write set SHALL NOT count as an available design for such a request: it SHALL become the same `unknown` design duty owned by the design phase as a missing artifact does, so the gap holds the implementation phase back, instead of leaving an implementation duty with no source behind. A feature with no resolvable acceptance source SHALL still carry an `acceptance-context` duty as `unknown` so the gap reaches its owner; the same holds for a missing design source and its `design-context` duty. The entry SHALL NOT fabricate a blueprint and SHALL NOT silently omit either duty. For a feature that has no blueprint artifacts at all, the requirement itself SHALL be the source: it is resolved through the existing requirement provider and bound like any other input. Such a request SHALL still produce a usable candidate — the definition gaps hold the implementation back through the existing gap path, and the birth chain contains only the investigating phases — rather than being refused at generation time. Refusal is reserved for a request that skips the design phases entirely and still has no verifiable write set. When the requested action is not given explicitly, the entry SHALL refuse and print the existing per-phase evidence facts (evidence integrity, freshness, phase verdict and closure status) instead of guessing an action; no action classifier SHALL be introduced.

Every candidate SHALL carry the requirement it was computed for as a machine-resolved binding — provenance, not documentation. At freeze time that binding SHALL be re-resolved against the requirement the run is actually born with: a fork between the two texts, a removed binding, or a substituted one SHALL refuse the freeze through the existing binding-verification path. The binding SHALL first be checked for shape: only the requirement input resolved through the requirement provider counts as provenance, so another legitimate binding of the same feature cannot be substituted for it and pass on its own re-resolution. A reader that holds no requirement text — the change-unit handoff projection, which freezes nothing — SHALL verify the binding's containment and dependency consistency and SHALL NOT invent a substitute text to compare against. Every entry that creates a run SHALL pass the run's own requirement when it has one; a run created without a requirement (an existing allowance) has no text to compare against and keeps only the containment and consistency checks. The candidate entry and the run-creation entry SHALL be mutually exclusive in a single invocation, so a candidate step can never silently create a run.

Regeneration with the same inputs SHALL leave the candidate byte-identical and SHALL NOT rewrite it. A candidate that differs from what the entry would generate SHALL be reported, not silently overwritten; overwriting SHALL require an explicit flag. The entry SHALL print the resolver's own projection (phase chain, each duty's applicability and reason, unresolved gaps) plus a templated explanation derived from that projection — a projection, not a model call. The user-visible next step SHALL continue to be rendered by the existing assess → NEXT_STEP renderer, which consumes the effective scope, and SHALL NOT present out-of-scope duties.

Enforcement: `harness/scripts/goal-mode-entry.ts`, `harness/scripts/utils/feature-track.ts`, `harness/scripts/utils/capability-resolution.ts`, `harness/scripts/utils/execution-scope.ts`, `harness/scripts/utils/assess-renderer.ts`.

#### Scenario: A verification-only request carries no implementation duty
- **WHEN** the requested action lists only verification phases for an existing implementation
- **THEN** the generated candidate SHALL contain no `implementation` duty and the resolved chain SHALL contain only those verification phases

#### Scenario: A missing acceptance source stays a visible gap
- **WHEN** the feature has no resolvable acceptance artifact or blueprint acceptance
- **THEN** the candidate SHALL carry an `unknown` acceptance duty that resolves into the unresolved list owned by spec, instead of omitting the duty

#### Scenario: A feature with only a requirement still gets a usable candidate
- **WHEN** the feature has no design or acceptance artifact and the request asks for full delivery
- **THEN** the candidate SHALL bind the requirement as the source of both `unknown` duties, the birth chain SHALL contain only the investigating phases, and the implementation duty SHALL appear in the gaps' `needed_by` instead of blocking generation

#### Scenario: A candidate cannot be reused for a different requirement
- **WHEN** the run is created with a requirement other than the one the candidate was generated for, or the candidate's requirement binding was removed, replaced, or swapped for another legitimate binding of the same feature
- **THEN** the freeze SHALL be refused rather than silently adopting the new requirement

#### Scenario: A design artifact with no write set is a design gap, not an implementation duty
- **WHEN** the design artifact exists but declares no verifiable write set and the request asks for both the design phase and the implementation phase
- **THEN** the design duty SHALL be `unknown` and owned by the design phase, and the implementation phase SHALL appear in the gap's `needed_by` instead of in the birth chain

#### Scenario: A hand-edited candidate is reported instead of overwritten
- **WHEN** the candidate on disk differs from what the same inputs would generate
- **THEN** the entry SHALL report the difference and leave the file untouched unless an explicit overwrite is requested
